episodes.212543: Isolated thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall during the late afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.212554: Slow-moving thunderstorms over Central Alabama dumped heavy rainfall in short periods of time during the afternoon and evening hours of June 7. Flash flooding issues developed in the Gadsden and Birmingham areas as 1-3 inches of rain fell quickly, with numerous flooding reports from urban or low-lying roadways. In addition, numerous trees and several power lines were downed around Gadsden and Attalla, caused by sub-severe winds aided by heavy rain and water-logged soils.
episodes.212557: On the 6th afternoon to early evening, a moist column combined with dynamic lift from an approaching cool front to produce numerous to widespread training thunderstorms over northern portions of central Indiana.  While most cells were generally sub-severe, isolated damaging winds were most organized in Warren County and most intense at the Muncie airport.  More noteworthy was the quasi-parallel nature of the approaching boundary to the moist conveyor's axis, which produced multiple roudns of heavy rain over several zones, and considerable flash flooding in portions of Warren County and Fountain County where up to an estimated 7.00 inches of rain fell. This severe weather event would be the first of many for the month which would eventually define a formal disaster period from June 6th to the 18th which was declared by the governor of Indiana.
episodes.212560: A low pressure system moved into the region, generating thunderstorms, some of which became severe over portions of northeast Montana.
episodes.212561: A low pressure system moved through the region and spread thunderstorms across far eastern Montana, a few of which became severe.
episodes.212566: A cold front swung through the area in the evening kicking off mostly sub severe storms, though a few did produce damaging winds in MA and CT.
episodes.212588: A thunderstorm producing heavy rain developed over portions of Lawrence County on June 7, 2026. This heavy rain in a short period of time caused nearby creeks to overfill their banks which caused flooding on a roadway.
episodes.212738: Ahead of an approaching cold front and aided by leading shortwave-induced ascent, a cluster of thunderstorms tracked across southeastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania producing wind damage, several tornadoes, and a few instances of large hail. Moist southerly flow pulled upper 50s to low 60s dew points with surface temperatures in the mid 70s allowing for sufficient destabilization up to 1500 J/kg of MLCAPE, 35-40 knots of effective shear, and 50-150 m2/s2 of 0-1 km SRH to support an all hazards threat.
episodes.212873: Thunderstorms developed off the higher terrain of eastern New Mexico on the afternoon of the sixth. Strong northwest flow behind a departing upper level low and a favorable moisture environment across West Texas allowed storms to persist into the South Plains on the evening of the sixth. These storms formed a small bow echo like feature with the apex of the bow impinging into western Lubbock County. A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Reese measured a severe wind gust to 71 mph. Additionally, an NWS storm survey revealed outbuildings that had been destroyed as well as roofs that had been blown off homes in western Lubbock County.
episodes.213127: During the morning of June 7th, training thunderstorms caused flooding across nearly the entire southern half of Boone County. Most of the flooding consisted of inches of water over roadways and flooded creeks. That afternoon through evening, additional thunderstorms exacerbated the problem, creating even more dangerous conditions through the morning of the 8th.
episodes.213164: Severe thunderstorms swept through the Missouri Ozarks during the evening and overnight hours of June 7th and 8th. Several tornadoes occurred along with significant flash flooding. Between 2 and 6 inches of rainfall fell over a short period of time across portions of southwest Missouri.
episodes.213192: Following two rounds of showers and thunderstorms in the morning, a third round later in the day produced damaging wind gusts over northwest Ohio.
episodes.213271: A slow-moving upper low and increasing moisture content contributed to a period of active weather during the weekend of June 5, with scattered showers and thunderstorms occurring across the area mainly in the evening and overnight hours. Flash flooding was the primary weather hazard throughout the weekend, along with isolated instances of hail and damaging winds.
episodes.213485: Several rounds of heavy rain spread over eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois the morning and afternoon hours June 7th, this brought flash flooding to a few areas in eastern Iowa and Illinois.
episodes.213492: Several rounds of heavy rain spread over eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois the morning and afternoon hours June 7th, this brought flash flooding to a few areas in eastern Iowa and Illinois.
episodes.213600: Low pressure located over western Nebraska featured a northward progressing warm front that extended as far as the Minnesota and Iowa border. On June 7th, 2026, this warm front proceeded into southern Minnesota which produced tropical-like precipitable water values exceeding 1.75 inches and dew points near 70 degrees. With sufficient instability in place, storms developed in the wake of the passing warm front.  Very heavy rainfall rates between 1.75 to 2.0 inches per hour produced localized flooding in Steele County. Two intersections were closed by law enforcement due to the flooding, and another rural intersection one mile south of Steele Center (CR-45 and 88th St) was closed due to moving water over the road.
episodes.213636: A few thunderstorms across far southeast Wyoming produced isolated strong wind gusts up to 66 MPH.
episodes.213637: A cold front pushed south across the area resulting in widely scattered severe thunderstorms over western Nebraska during the evening and late evening hours. Mostly strong gusty winds were reported along with small hail. A landspout tornado was also reported earlier in the afternoon.
episodes.213977: A broken band of thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the evening of the 6th, as an upper level disturbance approached the region. Low level wind shear increased with the approach of the disturbance, and this wind shear combined with a moderately unstable air mass that had developed, resulted in some of the storms developing low level rotation, which supported the formation of three tornadoes across Sebastian and Crawford Counties.
episodes.214050: A cluster of thunderstorms developed over northern Illinois during the pre-dawn hours of June 6th, then dropped southeastward into central Indiana as the morning progressed.  The storms skirted through Vermilion County with gusty winds and rain, but no reports of severe weather or flooding.  By late afternoon, thunderstorms began re-developing along the residual outflow boundary...with cells continuously back-building over portions of Vermilion County into the evening.  Very heavy rainfall occurred in a small portion of the county from Bismarck to the northern edge of Danville.  The Danville Airport (KDNV) measured 6.41, while an observer 1 mile west-northwest of the airport received 7.50.  The heavy rain falling on already wet soils led to flash flooding during the evening, with residual flooding lingering into the morning of June 7th.  Water rescues had to be performed near Stoney Creek on the southeast side of Danville as the creek overflowed its banks and flooded a few homes.
episodes.214344: Daytime-to-evening thunderstorm activity occurred on the north/east periphery of a persistent closed low across Texas on the 6th. Several more damaging downburst wind events occurred, including near Ada, OK. Slow-moving thunderstorms also produced reports of flooding in west-central Oklahoma during the evening hours.
episodes.214345: A slow-moving thunderstorm cluster impacted portions of western-north Texas during the predawn to mid-morning hours on the 7th. Combined with rich boundary layer moisture and occasional back-building convection, scattered instances of flash flooding occurred.
episodes.214511: A weak upper level system combined with a stalled frontal boundary extending over portions of southeast Louisiana and coastal Mississippi to produce a period of training thunderstorms over parts of Harrison, Hancock, and Pearl River Counties in coastal Mississippi.  Very high moisture content in the atmosphere and warm air in the mid and upper levels allowed for very high rainfall rates to accompany these training thunderstorms resulting in flash flooding.
episodes.214513: A weak upper level system combined with a stalled seabreeze boundary extending over portions of coastal Mississippi to produce a period of training thunderstorms over parts of the coastal waters. A few of these thunderstorms became strong enough to produce some severe marine wind gusts.
episodes.214590: A surface trough moved through North Dakota during the evening, with a few severe thunderstorms that occurred in northwest North Dakota. The largest hail report of ping pong ball sized hail was in Divide County. There were non-severe thunderstorms further south in Billings County near Fairfield, although there was a non-thunderstorm wind gust of 66 mph near Fairfield due to a heat burst. This caused the temperature to jump to 92 degrees.
episodes.214591: An upper level low and surface cold front combined with a very unstable airmass resulted in severe thunderstorms across western and central North Dakota. Supercell thunderstorms initially produced very large hail before transitioning to a linear storm mode, which led to widespread significant thunderstorm wind gusts. The largest reported hail was 3 inches in diameter, occurring southwest of Medora in Billings County. Measured wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph were common as storms moved across western and central North Dakota. The area with the most significant wind damage occurred across Stark, Morton, Mercer, and McLean Counties. In a swath from Dickinson, to Hebron, to Beulah, to Douglas Bay, to west of Garrison, damage from thunderstorm wind gusts led to winds estimated from 80 to 100 mph. The strongest measured wind gust came from a personal weather station just east of Beulah that reported a gust of 103 mph. Damage included campers turned over, large trees downed, roof damage, power outages, garages destroyed, vehicle damage, siding damage, and dented grain bins.
episodes.214678: A surface trough with an approaching upper level short-wave trough would lead to damaging winds and flash flooding across west-central Arkansas.
episodes.214695: An unsettled weather pattern unfolded across the Ohio Valley and Central Appalachians for the start of June amid a stalled frontal boundary and building heat and humidity. This combination allowed for daily storm initiation across the Midwest that eventually tracked into Ohio and northern West Virginia. On June 6th and 7th, storms tracking into the area reached Harrison and Taylor Counties late in the evening and caused tree and power line damage before dissipating with the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.214707: A weak upper level disturbance traversed east-northeast across the Red River Valley and North Texas into Southwest Arkansas and extreme Northwest Louisiana during the late evening through the overnight hours of June 6th-7th, across a warm, moist, and unstable air mass already in place. Large scale forcing coupled with adequate wind shear contributed to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across these areas, with a couple of isolated severe thunderstorms producing damaging winds that downed a couple of trees in Southern Howard County Arkansas and Northeast Wood County Texas.
episodes.214708: A weak upper level disturbance traversed east-northeast across the Red River Valley and North Texas into Southwest Arkansas and extreme Northwest Louisiana during the late evening through the overnight hours of June 6th-7th, across a warm, moist, and unstable air mass already in place. Large scale forcing coupled with adequate wind shear contributed to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across these areas, with a couple of isolated severe thunderstorms producing damaging winds that downed a couple of trees in Southern Howard County Arkansas and Northeast Wood County Texas.
episodes.215004: Isolated storms produced minor severe weather across western SD.
episodes.215006: More organized thunderstorms developed and a few supecell storms managed to get going across northwestern SD. These supercells were responsible for large hail (+2) and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215046: An upper level trough and associated surface cold front approached from the west. Out ahead of the cold front, a pre-frontal trough moved through the area. The pre-frontal trough sparked convection in an area characterized by about 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE and 35 kt of 0-6km bulk shear. Several severe thunderstorms formed and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215053: An upper level trough and associated surface cold front approached from the west. Out ahead of the cold front, a pre-frontal trough moved through the area. The pre-frontal trough sparked convection in an area characterized by about 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE and 35 kt of 0-6km bulk shear. Several severe thunderstorms formed and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215055: An upper level trough and associated surface cold front approached from the west. Out ahead of the cold front, a pre-frontal trough moved through the area. The pre-frontal trough sparked convection in an area characterized by about 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE and 35 kt of 0-6km bulk shear. Several severe thunderstorms formed and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215066: Severe thunderstorms brought damaging winds to eastern Wyoming.
episodes.215089: A weak upper-level low moved from west Texas into Oklahoma. With a warm, moist airmass in place over South-Central Texas the disturbance generated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215155: High based showers developed in an area of very dry surface air and large dew point depressions. This led to some very strong wind gusts when showers collapsed.
episodes.215242: A cold front moved across western and central Wyoming and brought a scattering of showers and thunderstorms. With large dew point depressions and supportive upper level dynamics, strong wind gusts occurred across much of central Wyoming. The most widespread high wind gusts were in Johnson County. After the cold front passage, a brief period of high wind driven by a tight pressure gradient and northwest flow brought strong synoptic winds to Johnson County.
episodes.215526: A shortwave moving through aloft along with a surface cold front was able to spark isolated showers and thunderstorms. One storm became severe and produced a damaging wind gust over the waters.
episodes.215610: Scattered afternoon storms developed across southeast Texas with a couple storms becoming severe.
episodes.215620: A line of storms developed along a trough axis during the evening hours on June 6, resulting in multiple reports of thunderstorm wind damage.
episodes.215753: A large mid-level trough pushed through the Pacific NW into the northern Great Basin throughout June 6-8, bringing a few scattered severe wind gusts to Tooele county.
episodes.215809: On the afternoon of June sixth a progressive shortwave trough approached New Hampshire from Vermont.  This brought moderate instability aloft along with deep level shear.  These ingredients interacted with a hot and humid day for early June that led to amble CAPE that could support severe thunderstorm outflow winds.  A line of storms developed in Vermont and progressed across the Connecticut River Valley into New Hampshire bringing with it gusty outflow winds that brought down trees.
episodes.216098: Multiple severe storms occurred, producing winds up to 67 mph and hail up to 3 inches in diameter. Some minor flooding occurred as well.
episodes.216099: Multiple severe storms occurred, producing winds up to 67 mph and hail up to 3 inches in diameter. Some minor flooding occurred as well.
episodes.216446: An upper-level trough moving through the region combined with cooling temperatures aloft and daytime heating to facilitate shower and thunderstorm activity. A shower was strong enough to produce a cold-air funnel along the coast in addition to a short lived thunderstorm producing strong outflow winds in southwest Washington.

An unusually intense storm was able to generate a strong downdraft despite limited environmental support, which resulted in a narrow damage swath in Meadow Glade, WA in Clark County. NWS Portland conducted a damage survey in the affected area on Sunday, June 7. NWS storm surveyors found a small area at the  west end of the storm track which experienced heavier damage,  including a metal roof peeled back from an outbuilding and  multiple hardwood trees with trunks snapped multiple feet above  ground level. These damage indicators suggest a maximum wind speed  of just over 90 mph. As the storm moved east, associated wind  speeds weakened, producing minor damage including small downed or  broken tree limbs, lifted roof shingles, and damaged fences,  corresponding to wind speeds of 50-65 mph.
